title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
abstract: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.
summary: This paper introduces a sophisticated homotopy-theoretic framework to define 't Hooft anomalies and higher symmetries in quantum systems. It uses crossed precosheaves to build a $\check{	ext{C}}$ech-Loday classifying space that captures the full structure of localized symmetries. This provides a powerful, general tool for classifying topological invariants in condensed matter and quantum field theory.
main_problem: To develop a rigorous, homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies and higher symmetries in quantum field theories and lattice models, moving beyond group-theoretic descriptions.
main_result: The authors construct the $\check{	ext{C}}$ech-Loday classifying space, $\check{BF}(\xi)$, whose structure encodes higher symmetry groups and whose non-triviality detects anomalies that obstruct gauging.
method: The method involves using crossed precosheaves of groups attached to spatial regions and constructing the associated $\check{	ext{C}}$ech-Loday classifying complex, which is a pro-object in the homotopy category.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general quantum field theories and quantum lattice models, with specific examples given for quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, and quantum cellular automata.
key_observables: The anomaly is detected by the homotopy class of the map $\kappa_F(\xi) \circ Bho: BG 	o \check{BF}(\xi)$; higher symmetries are encoded in the homotopy groups of $\check{BF}(\xi)$.
important_parameters: The structure depends on the crossed precosheaf $\xi$, which captures localized symmetries and their non-abelian commutation relations.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the structure of crossed precosheaves, which are necessary because physical symmetries often violate the simple multiplicative partition of unity assumption.
paper_structure: The paper develops the framework by defining the crossed precosheaf, constructing the $\check{	ext{C}}$ech-Loday classifying space, and then applying this machinery to derive known invariants (like the Else-Nayak index) for specific physical models.
why_interesting: The framework provides powerful topological tools to classify robust, non-local symmetries in quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding topological phases of matter relevant to correlated electron physics.
